ada: Heads-up — saw a pretty consistent NDCG drop after running PTQ on the v2 reranker when docs exceed ~1k tokens. Posting numbers now.
manuel: Can you paste the eval command, dataset, and the exact quant config?
ada: Eval command: `python eval_rerank.py --model rerank-v2-ptq --data org-queries-2025.jsonl --truncate 1024 --batch 64`
ada: Baseline float32 NDCG@10 = 0.832. PTQ run = 0.801. MRR dropped ~3.2%.
shreya: Are you sure truncation is applied at the same stage as the float run? Tokenization or passage splitting order can move boundaries.
manuel: Also check whether truncation happens before or after doc->passage split. We had a bug last year that truncated raw doc and then split, instead of splitting then truncating passages.
ada: Good call — current loader truncates raw doc first (`loader.truncate_text()`), so passages are shorter.
c i-bot: Build r23: tests passed for eval harness.
tom: Try `--truncate 2048` and `--no-trunc` to get a length curve. Also try aligning the float run to the same preprocessing.
ada: Ran `--truncate 2048` -> NDCG@10 = 0.828. Ran `--no-trunc` (keep full text, split with sliding window) -> NDCG@10 = 0.831. So larger context helps, but PTQ still trails fp32.
shreya: That smells like quantization sensitivity to long-context hidden states. Which PTQ mode? Per-channel? Symmetric?
ada: Using internal PTQ pipeline: `ptq.mode=static`, `ptq.per_channel=false`, `bitwidth=8`, `quantize_bias=false`.
manuel: Try `ptq.per_channel=true` and also run asymmetric quantization on activations. Those reduce layerwise bias for MatMuls.
ada: Will queue those.
ada: Also found ~0.7% of queries in dataset with stray `\n` characters and trailing spaces in `query_text`. Could affect prefix keys and caching behavior.
shreya: Nice catch. Formatting differences between dataset versions can create subtle distribution shifts. Clean and re-run.
ada: After cleaning queries and switching to `ptq.per_channel=true`: NDCG@10 = 0.825, MRR = 0.826. Gap reduced but still ~0.006–0.007 below fp32.
manuel: Small remaining gap — could be noise. What's bootstrap CI?
ada: Bootstrapped 1000 samples: fp32 0.832 ±0.003, ptq 0.825 ±0.0035. Non overlapping but close.
shreya: Let's also test with a holdout subset of short docs (<512 tokens) vs long docs (>2048). If PTQ degradation is concentrated in long docs that's actionable.
tom: Agreed. Also try per-layer sensitivity: quantize only attention or only FFN to isolate.
ada: Plan: 1) run ptq.per_channel variant, 2) split long/short doc evals, 3) ablate quant on attention vs ffn, 4) verify preprocessing parity with float.
manuel: Add a note to the eval checklist to always include `--preproc-seed` and `--preproc-mode` flags so we can ensure identical splits next time.
ada: Will update the runbook and push a quick script to canonicalize query fields.
ada: Quick snippet I used to clean queries: ```python
for r in dataset:
    r['query_text'] = r['query_text'].strip().replace('\n',' ')
    r['query_text'] = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', r['query_text'])
```
shreya: Thanks — can you attach the cleaned dataset sha once it's uploaded?
ad a: :thinking: (reaction)
ada: Uploaded cleaned shard to s3://redwood-eval/cleans/org-queries-2025-cleaned-v1.jsonl sha256: a3f4...
shreya: Once we have per-layer ablation numbers we can decide if we need per-channel PTQ in the serving build or fallback to mixed precision on long docs.
tom: If per-layer shows attention is most sensitive, consider keeping attention in fp16 and quantizing FFN. That often preserves ranking.
manuel: Agree. Add a quick A/B plan for dedicated vs hosted customers if we change default quant policy.
ada: Will post results in this thread once ablations finish (~2 hrs). :rocket:
ci-bot: rerank-eval job queued (#r24).
